messages.body_plain:
Hi,

thanks for letting me know.  I managed to reproduce that problem, but
it really puzzles me why it occurs.  That code, digest::digest(...,
skip = skip, ascii = ascii), is only used if you have digest v0.3.0
(tested for), which is yet not publically available, and you certainly
have v0.2.3.  So, it shouldn't be called, but for some reason it is.
I'll track it down.

Workaround, because I'm prepared for my own mistakes ;), is to do:

options("aroma.affymetrix::assertDigest"=FALSE)
library(aroma.affymetrix)
digest <- .digest.fix023

...and then it should work as usual.

Henrik

> I've added method gc() to instances of class Object (which all
> aroma.affymetrix class inherits from) so when called like you do, e.g.
> gc(csN), it will clear all cached fields of object 'csN' and the call
> the global gc().  You'll see this if you do:
>
>
>> print(gc.Object)
>>
>
> function (this, ...)
> {
>     clearCache(this)
>     gc()
> }
>
> On the other hand, the global gc() [now renamed to gc.default()] is
> defined in the base package and does exactly what it used to do;
> garbage collect R's internal memory.  It does *not* recursively call
> gc() on Object:s, because first there is no way to add so called hooks
> for this, but also because it would be too expensive to do this each
> time the garbage collector is in action.  Also, cached values in
> Object:s are not memory garbage in the common sense; we cache values
> for a purpose and might want to reuse them, i.e. they should be
> removed only when we explicitly say so.  On the other hand, regular
> memory garbage are objects lost for ever that we never can reuse.  It
> might be that another name than gc() for Object:s would be more
> appropriate; I just though it was a short convenient name and related
> to gc().  As seen above, you can perfectly well just do:
>
>  clearCache(csN)
>
> which maybe makes more sense.
>
> If you are interested in exactly what makes an Object large, you can
> use the ll() (two L:s) function.  Since cached fields are "private"
> (prefixed with a dot), you have to do:
>
> ll(csN, private=TRUE)

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")

install.packages("aroma.affymetrix_0.4.4.tar.gz", repos=NULL)
install.packages("aroma.affymetrix_0.4.4.zip", repos=NULL)

explain this too.

it.  Feedback is valuable and helps finding the bug(s) so please keep
sending them.

Henrik

The XDA CEL file format is the formal name for what we normally call
"binary" CEL files.  See ?affxparser.  See also Section "1.
Dictionary" in the HTML help of affxparser.

These files should do for you.

>
> AGCC Flat Files: This zip file contains AGCC format CEL files and AGCC
> ARR sample attribute files generated from the GCOS Flat Files. These
> files are intended for use with Expression Console and other Exon
> Array analysis software. They are not intended for import into GCOS
> systems. The files were generated using a beta version of DEC
> (software for converting files).

I do not know what "AGCC" stands for, but I know that "CC" have be
used for "Command Console files" which to the best of my knowledge is
also going under the work name "Calvin" files.  Calvin is a new more
generic binary format from Affymetrix which is more flexible and more
generic, cf. XML.  I'm not sure how well the standardized CEL files
are for this format; they are migrating towards using it (see e.g.
http://www.affymetrix.com/support/developer/apt_download/apt_changelog.affx),
but although affxparser should be able to read such CEL files out of
the box (it does on the few we tested), I would stick we the standard
binary files for now.

  missing.  Now it is instead created.

  error about too many open connections.

  that was supposed to be if (!fource) {} in the release version.

  to return a ResidualSet containing AffymetrixCelFile:s.  The same

createExpressionTable<-function(chp.unm) {
  x<-readUnits(chp.unm)
  t.nm<-names(x)
  x.ul<-unlist(x)
  nc<-nbrOfArrays(chp.nomerge)
  ex.data<-t(matrix(x.ul,nrow=nc))  # get exon intensities
  rn<-NULL
  for(i in 1:length(t.nm)) {
    rn<-c(rn,paste(names(x)[i],names(x[[i]]),sep="."))
    if( i %% 100 == 0 ) { print(i) }
  }
  rownames(ex.data)<-rn
  colnames(ex.data)<-getNames(chp.unm)
  ex.data

> want. But now I want to transfer my analysis temporarily to another
> computer and don't want to have to copy all the CEL files for the
> previous versions of the data and I'm not sure how to create a reference
> to the quantile normalized data without the earlier steps.
>
> I think I should use either AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles or
> AffymetrixCelSet$fromName, but I'm not sure what arguments I need to put
> in and there's no help page for these functions (I can look at 'args()'
> but there are '...' that I think need to be filled in that I don't
> know). The examples I know are for the raw data with no tags, etc., so
> I'm not sure how to do it more generally.

Both

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles(path)

and

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(dataSetName, tags=tags, chipType=chipType)

would do.  I prefer the former since there you explicitly specify the
path to the the directory containing the CEL files.  The second one is
searching for the the CEL set under rawData/ and probeData/.

About documentation/help/args():  A lot of the arguments are passed to
the same method in a superclass via '...'.  The reason why I do this
is to keep redundancy and therefore maintenance low.   I could repeat
the arguments of interest and pass them down internally, but if I
change default values etc there is a risk for inconsistency.  When
this part of the package stabilizes, I might consider doing that, or
find an improved, say, argsS3(), that backtrack all possible
arguments.  That's in the future.

>
> The path of the folder with my quantile normalized data would be
> "..\probeData\Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,QN\HuEx-1_0-st-v2\". If both can do
> it, it would be nice to see what a 'best' call to the two functions
> would look like for future reference.

I think that should be

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles("../probeData/Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,QN/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/")

I'm a bit puzzled about the '../' part.  The package is design such
that it expect rawData/, probeData/, plmData/ etc to be in the
*current* directory.  But, yes, you can access another path using the
static fromFiles() method.  The fromName() alternative would be:

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("Affy_tissue_comm", tags="RBC,QN",
chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2", paths="../probeData/")

where 'paths' had to be specified explicitly in the 2nd case because
the CEL set is not under one of the standard paths.  In other words,
please do no rely on this, because one of the strengths in the designs
of aroma.affymetrix is to have a strict directory setup.  It make many
things much easier.

A much better way is to create a link, or a Windows Shortcut in your
case, letting

  probeData\Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,QN\

point to

 ..\probeData\Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,QN\

You can easily do that in Windows Explorer.

Hope this helps

Henrik

>
> Thanks,
> Elizabeth

CDF files are in so called "Library files", which are zipped archives.
You'll find the under the "Support Materials" page for each of the
chip types/sets on the Affymetrix site.

FYI: I've added the two chip types under Section "Documentation on
chip types" in "Pages" on the group page.

> how would I get a CDF for that ... or what package do I use to make
> one from the Bioconductor packages.  I could, of course, process this
> with the normal packages.

As above.

Note, the CDFs for the above chip types are all provided as ASCII CDF
files.  Since it is *much* faster to work with binary CDFs, make sure
to convert the files to binary CDF files first.  Use convertCdf() in
affxparser for this.  See ?convertCdf for more help.
